trust_decision.summary: Only the VM's main user may connect to the root-run guest-agent gRPC socket /run/lima-guestagent.sock; at the pinned commit daemonAction creates it root-owned with mode 0777, so every local guest user is authorized to the root agent.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the guest-agent socket, and this os.Chmod(socket, 0o777) is the only place in the tree that sets that socket's mode, so an engineer starts here.

fix_sites.entry_point: guest boot script run from cloud-init user-data (openrc branch)
guest boot script run from cloud-init user-data (systemd branch)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The openrc branch is a separate, non-default (Alpine) service implementation in a shell template, and the boot script looks like mere plumbing, so a solver can argue the daemon-side chmod is the whole security fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The host dials the guest socket as the main user through an SSH local forward and the daemon must keep running as root for iptables; a 0600-only (root-owned) socket makes the agent unreachable, and running the daemon unprivileged breaks port forwarding.

O6_input_shapes: socket-owner > 0 (main user UID): chown the socket then chmod 0600
socket-owner absent or 0 (root): chmod 0600 only, no chown
systemd launch via install-systemd: the UID must be serialized into the generated unit's ExecStart args
openrc launch via the boot script: the UID must be passed directly on the daemon command line
unix-socket transport (no vsock/virtio port) vs vsock/virtio transports: only the unix-socket branch needs an owner

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second listener branch (e.g. a debug vsock listener or a runtime-dir control socket) that is not wrapped in cidFilteredListener and is not chowned to the main user.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already branches per transport and already carries a CID filter; a maintainer adding a debug/alternate transport would naturally copy this branch and forget the access restriction.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second service-definition generator (launchd plist, SysV init script or systemd user unit) that launches daemon without --socket-owner.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Lima already supports macOS guests and several init systems, so per-init generators beside the embedded systemd template are a natural addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third launcher branch (no-init/SysV or a rootless user service) that runs `lima-guestagent daemon` without --socket-owner.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The boot script already special-cases openrc versus systemd; adding another distro branch there is exactly how the existing two were written.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A host-side creation of the forwarded ga.sock (instead of letting ssh create it) with a permissive mode, exposing the guest agent to other host users.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The host mirrors the guest socket path and already removes/re-creates it on reconnect, so an explicit local bind with a default umask is a plausible maintainer change.

O9_family: CWE-276 / CWE-668: incorrect default permissions on a root-owned unix socket, exposing the guest agent to every local user (local privilege escalation)

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.25.7 per go.mod; make; shellcheck/shfmt for the .sh templates
O10_build.project_tests: CI runs `go test -v ./...` (.github/workflows/test.yml:153); there are no unit tests in cmd/lima-guestagent, pkg/cidata has template-render tests only, and the boot script is covered by make shellcheck/shfmt (Makefile:633-639), not behaviourally

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change os.Chmod(socket, 0o777) to 0o600 in daemonAction and stop; the socket is then root-owned and the main user's SSH forward can no longer connect.

out_of_scope_notes: pkg/portfwdserver/server.go:38 dials a protocol/address supplied over the guest-agent gRPC stream; that is a capability of the protected sink, not part of this advisory, and was not pursued.
The host-side forwarded socket ${LIMA_HOME}/<inst>/ga.sock relies on the instance dir being 0700 (pkg/instance/create.go:65); outside this advisory and not pursued.

website/content/en/docs/dev/internals.md:93 says qemu uses virtio-port, but pkg/driver/qemu/qemu_driver.go:57-68 leaves the virtio port empty on non-Windows hosts; the doc looks stale, not a vulnerability.
